diagnostic_evidence.quote: I_y &\lesssim h^4 \int_{\HH} \left\{ \sum_{k=0}^4 \left(x_2^{k-3} \partial_{x_2}^k v(\x)\right)^2 + \sum_{k=0}^2 \left(x_2^{k-2}\partial_{x_1}\partial_{x_2}^k v(\x)\right)^2 + h^2  \sum_{k=0}^4 \left(x_2^{k-4} \partial_{x_2}^k v(\x)\right)^2 \right\} \dd{\x}

issues.failure_explanation: Writing w=v/x_2^2 and w_\pm=w(x_1,x_2\pm h), the integrand of I_y is \sum_\pm((j\pm1)^2-1/4)w_\pm - 2(j^2-1/4)w - \partial_{x_2}^2 v. Since (j\pm1)^2-1/4=(j^2-1/4)\pm 2j+1 and \partial_{x_2}^2 v = x_2^2 w''+4x_2 w'+2w, the integrand equals (j^2-1/4)(w_++w_--2w) - x_2^2 w'' + 2j(w_+-w_-) - 4x_2 w' + (w_++w_--2w). The proof's rewriting drops the last term (w_++w_--2w) = h^2 w'' + O(h^4 w''''), so the subsequent Taylor expansion and estimates of I_y are performed on an incorrect expression. Additionally, the h^2 x_2^{-2}(x_2^2\partial_{x_1}w'')^2 contribution appearing in the penultimate display is absent from \eqref{eq:estimate-first-lapl-Iy}, and the final bound is stated with the Euclidean measure d\x while C^v copies the same x_2 exponents into L^2(\HH) (hyperbolic measure) norms, so the stated C^v does not match what the proof produces (exponents off by one).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reinstate the term (w_++w_--2w) in the I_y decomposition, expand it by Lemma lem:croytoru_integral (giving h^2 w'' plus a fourth-order remainder), estimate it by Cauchy–Schwarz as for the other terms, and correct the exponents / add the missing mixed-derivative terms in the definition of C^v (all remaining bounded by \|v\|_{\mathcal{M}_\gamma}).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the O(h^2) consistency estimate for the first discrete Laplacian is not correct as written; the missing term contributes (j^2-1/4)\{\int_{\CC} h^2 w''\}^2 \lesssim h^4\int x_2^2 (w'')^2 dx, which is of the same order as the retained terms and is controlled by the same weighted norms, so the conclusion Err_h(v)\lesssim C^v h^2 with C^v \lesssim \|v\|_{\mathcal{M}_\gamma} survives, but with a corrected C^v.
issues.title: Missing term in the I_y decomposition of the first-Laplacian consistency proof (and inconsistent bookkeeping of C^v)
issues.why_classification: A short local recomputation restores the argument; the rate O(h^2), the method, and the bound by the \mathcal{M}_\gamma norm are all preserved, only the bookkeeping constant C^v changes.

issues.failure_explanation: To obtain the O(h^2) bound one must show \|\Delta_g u(t)\|_{L^2(\HH\setminus\HHD)} \lesssim h^2 and the analogous bounds over \HH\setminus\mathbb{H}^2_{2/(5h)}. Corollary coro:tail-control-heat (via Lemma lem:tail-control and \eqref{eq:lem-2}) only controls weighted L^2 norms of u itself and only for D=D_{h,\gamma,\zeta}=\zeta h^{-\gamma} with \zeta>2; the paper establishes no exponentially weighted L^2 bound for second derivatives of u(t) (Lemma lem:2-relatii gives only polynomial x_2^s weights for derivatives), and 2/(5h) is not of the admitted form. The cited equations \eqref{eq:x_1-x_2-bound-by-exp} and \eqref{acaret:eq:Laplace-g-estimate-derivatives} do not close this gap. Hence the remark's proof relies on an unestablished premise.

failure_location.quote: By Corollary~\ref{coro:tail-control-heat}, taking into account equations~\eqref{eq:x_1-x_2-bound-by-exp} and~\eqref{acaret:eq:Laplace-g-estimate-derivatives}, we arrive at the desired consistency estimate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a short argument: write \Delta_g u(t)=e^{t\Delta_g}\Delta_g u_0+\int_0^t e^{(t-\sigma)\Delta_g}\Delta_g f(\sigma)d\sigma (\Delta_g commutes with the semigroup), apply Lemma lem:stability-exp(alpha-d) with \alpha=2+4/\gamma and bound e^{\alpha d_g}|\Delta_g u_0|\le 4e^{(\alpha+2)d_g}|\Delta_e u_0| via \eqref{eq:x_1-x_2-bound-by-exp}, which is controlled by \|u_0\|_{\mathcal{M}_\gamma} since \alpha+2\le\max\{18,4+4/\gamma\}; then apply the tail lemma. Handle D'=2/(5h) by the same lemma for h<1/5 and trivially for larger h.
issues.overall_effect: The bounded-domain consistency estimates (property (L3)) for both discrete Laplacians, and hence the fully discrete convergence theorem which invokes them, rest on an unproved step; the semi-discrete theorem thm:added-1 is unaffected as it is stated conditionally on (L3).
issues.title: Tail terms involving \Delta_g u and the strip \HH\setminus\mathbb{H}^2_{2/(5h)} are not covered by the cited tail-control corollary
issues.why_classification: The gap is closed by a short argument using only tools already in the paper (Duhamel, commutation, Lemma lem:stability-exp(alpha-d), Lemma lem:tail-control); all rates and claims survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, if $\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ (i.e., when we use the Crank-Nicolson scheme) and $T$ is an integral multiple of $\tau$, then the order of the convergence above is $\mathcal{O}(h^2+\tau^2)$.
Summing up these relations for $k\in \overline{0,(k_{\tau,T}-1)}$, where $k_{\tau,T}=\left\lfloor \frac{T}{\tau}\right\rfloor$

In consequence, we select the time step $\tau$ according to $\theta$, on the lines \ref{alg:ifTheta}-\ref{alg:elseTheta} of Algorithm \ref{alg:theta-heat-hyperbolic}, in order to ensure a convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ for our $\theta$-scheme, regardless of $\theta \in [1/2, 1]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop starts at k=0, updates U to the approximation at time (k+1)\tau, increments k, and stops only when k\tau>T. If T=K\tau is an integral multiple of \tau, the loop exits with k=K+1, so the output U approximates u((K+1)\tau)=u(T+\tau), not u(T); the resulting error contains \|u(T+\tau)-u(T)\|=O(\tau), contradicting the theorem's O(h^2+\tau^2) claim for \theta=1/2 precisely in the case it covers. The proof instead assumes the output is U^{k_{\tau,T}} with k_{\tau,T}=\lfloor T/\tau\rfloor, which is not what the pseudocode produces. Moreover, with \tau=h for \theta=1/2 nothing forces T/h\in\mathbb{N}, so the advertised O(h^2) 'regardless of \theta' only follows from the theorem under the integrality condition (otherwise only O(h^2+\tau)=O(h)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the stopping condition to k\tau \ge T (so the loop ends at k=T/\tau when T\in\tau\mathbb{N}), and for \theta=1/2 choose \tau=T/\lceil T/h\rceil (or state the integrality condition) so that the O(h^2+\tau^2) bound applies.
issues.overall_effect: The second (Crank–Nicolson, O(h^2+\tau^2)) statement of thm:convergence-theta does not hold for the output of the algorithm as literally written, and the unconditional O(h^2) rate for \theta=1/2 asserted in Section 7 and the conclusions is only established when T is a multiple of h.
issues.title: Time loop of Algorithm 1 overshoots the final time; O(tau^2) Crank–Nicolson claim not delivered by the algorithm as written
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of the loop condition and an explicit choice/condition on \tau restore full agreement between algorithm, theorem and prose; no rate or result is lost.
